palette.notes: Near-black void with a white starfield; grey cobble road; muted tiles (dark green, grey, rust/orange); knight in steel-blue with red boots and orange shield; lich in glowing pale cyan. Warm embers on cool blue-black. Critics cite an 80s look (wiki). No metrics file, so no count.

lighting: Mostly flat; the only light is glow: the lich and a golden saint figure carry a halo/aura and sparkle pixels, embers glow orange in the dark. Contrast between the black void and small lit shapes carries the mood.
silhouette: Gameplay assets are tiny but each tile and enemy type has a distinct chunky shape; promo art scales the knight and the lich up big against black so the silhouette (helmet plume, shield disc, hooded robe with staff) carries the character.

motion.timing: No metrics file. Most of the screen is still; the hero walks the loop on his own, battles open in a separate black panel where two rows of small combatants face off with HP bars above and damage numbers popping; the lich dissolves into scattered pixels.

texture: Heavy dithering and pixel noise on tiles (rubble, forests, rock), so the map looks gritty even when tiny; UI is chunky grey-metal frames and brown card borders.
camera: Fixed top-down view of the whole loop, no scrolling; battles appear as a framed inset panel over the map; card hand along the bottom.

acting.enters: The hero walks the loop on his own; enemies spawn on tiles the player placed; in the battle panel combatants are simply there, lined up facing each other.
acting.acts: Fights cut to a small framed panel: side-on rows, HP bars, red damage numbers, EVADE text; the boss lich floats and glows.
acting.exits: The hero retreats to camp between expeditions (per the wiki); defeated figures dissolve into pixels.
acting.depth: One flat plane; scale comes from cutting between the tiny map and the closer battle panel, and in promo art from a big hero close against a starfield.

techniques: near-black void + starfield as the background for everything
glow aura and sparkle pixels instead of modelled light
dithered noise texture on tiny tiles
cut to a framed inset panel for close-up action
side-on face-off rows with HP bars and popping damage numbers
dissolve into scattered pixels on defeat/exit
mostly static screen with one moving hero
feel: black void + tiny dithered tiles + glowing hero + rationed motion = moody, readable
for_fred: Keep Fred tiny walking a set path in the background while the main content runs, then cut to a small framed inset for his close-up gag; when he leaves, let him dissolve into scattered pixels instead of sliding off, so the exit itself is an event.
